La célèbre chouette verte ne fait plus rire tout le monde. Autrefois roi incontesté de l’apprentissage des langues, Duolingo traverse une zone de turbulences. Entre une refonte d'interface controversée, une obsession pour la monétisation et un virage « tout IA » qui déshumanise l'expérience, de nombreux utilisateurs se sentent trahis.
...
## Un chemin balisé qui ne laisse aucune place à la liberté

Pendant des années, le petit son de notification de Duolingo a rythmé mes journées. C’était le compagnon idéal pour apprendre quelques mots d’espagnol dans le métro ou réviser mon anglais avant de dormir. Mais depuis quelque temps, la magie n'opère plus. Ce qui était un jeu éducatif stimulant est devenu une corvée répétitive et frustrante. Et le pire, c'est que je ne suis pas le seul à le penser.

Le premier coup de poignard a été la mise à jour radicale de l'interface, transformant le célèbre « arbre » de compétences en un « chemin » (ou path) linéaire et interminable. Fini le temps où l’on pouvait choisir de renforcer tel ou tel aspect de la grammaire selon ses envies. Désormais, Duolingo vous prend par la main et ne vous lâche plus, vous forçant à suivre une route unique.

Cette simplification à outrance, censée guider les néophytes, a surtout aliéné les vétérans.

Les témoignages sont cinglants : « Ils ont officiellement ruiné leur application ». L'impossibilité de revenir en arrière facilement ou de cibler ses révisions donne l'impression d'être infantilisé. On ne clique plus pour apprendre, on clique pour faire avancer un pion, machinalement.

## La dictature des cœurs et de la gamification

Mais le plus agaçant reste sans doute la gestion punitive de l'erreur. Si vous utilisez la version gratuite, le système de « cœurs » est une aberration pédagogique. Faire une erreur devrait faire partie du processus d'apprentissage. Or, sur Duolingo, cinq erreurs et c'est la fin de la leçon, à moins de payer ou de regarder des publicités interminables.

Le résultat ? On finit par ne plus oser tenter des phrases complexes de peur de perdre une vie. On se contente de valider des acquis pour maintenir sa streak (cette fameuse série de jours consécutifs qui devient vite une source d'anxiété). Même les investisseurs commencent à tiquer. Bien que l'application affiche une croissance, celle-ci est en deçà des attentes (40% au lieu des 45% espérés), un signe que le modèle commence à s'essouffler face à la grogne des utilisateurs.

Voici un comparatif rapide pour comprendre comment l'application segmente désormais ses utilisateurs :

Duolingo (Gratuit) | Super Duolingo | Duolingo Max (IA)
...
Vies | Limitées (5 cœurs) | Illimitées | Illimitées 
Publicités | Fréquentes et intrusives | Aucune | Aucune 
Fonctionnalités IA | Aucune | Aucune | Jeux de rôle + Explications 
Prix | Gratuit | ~7,33€ / mois | ~12,49€ / mois 

## L'IA et la fin de l'aspect communautaire

Le coup de grâce pour les puristes a été le virage brutal vers l'intelligence artificielle, au détriment de l'humain. Récemment, l'entreprise a fait la une pour s'être séparée d'une partie de ses traducteurs contractuels au profit de l'IA, comme le rapportait Bloomberg.

Concrètement, cela se ressent dans la qualité des phrases, parfois lunaires, mais surtout dans la disparition de l'âme communautaire. Les forums de discussion, qui permettaient aux utilisateurs de s'entraider et de comprendre pourquoi une réponse était fausse, ont été fermés. À la place ? On vous vend désormais un abonnement « Max » pour qu'un chatbot vous explique vos erreurs. On a remplacé l'entraide gratuite par un robot payant. C'est peut-être brillant économiquement, mais c'est une perte immense pour l'apprentissage.

Aujourd'hui, je continue d'ouvrir l'application, plus par habitude que par passion. Mais si Duolingo continue de privilégier ses métriques d'engagement au détriment de la pédagogie réelle, il se pourrait bien que ma chouette finisse par définitivement disparaître de mon téléphone.

results.summary:
# Duolingo’s big course upgrade is making some learners feel lost

This wasn’t the Duolingo upgrade I had in mind.
...
Jul 8, 2026 — 2:26 PM ET
...
Megan Ellis / Android Authority

TL;DR

- The recent Duolingo course upgrade has left some learners complaining that their progress has been scrambled.
- Some users say completed units now include material they never learned, while others have been pushed back into basic lessons.
- Other users are also frustrated by the strict new flashcards that reject reasonable answers.

As a part of the increasing minority of people who haven’t yet given up on Duolingo, I laid out a bunch of changes I’d ideally like to see to improve the app last month. Well, Duolingo has indeed made some changes, but they aren’t the ones I wanted. Worse still, the recently introduced Duolingo course upgrade that the company implemented instead has infuriated a whole bunch of people online.

Several recent threads on the r/duolingo subreddit are full of users complaining that their language courses have been shuffled around in ways that make their progress hard to follow. In one thread, a user learning Italian said they had been at around level 50 and were working through more challenging material, only to find themselves suddenly being tested on basic words such as sugar, cat, tree, and milk. Other users in the same thread said they had run into similar issues with Japanese, German, and Spanish.

### Have the recent Duolingo course updates negatively impacted your progress?
...
The exact complaints vary, but the theme is familiar — Duolingo has rearranged the furniture, and some learners are now stumbling into tables. A few say they have been pushed backward into easy material, while others say the app is acting as if they have already learned words and grammar points they have never seen before.

As an example of that latter complaint, a German learner said lessons had been added retroactively to their path, with Duolingo treating unfamiliar material as if it had already been covered. Another commenter summed up the frustration neatly, saying they liked the idea of Duolingo improving and extending courses, but not that completed units were now filled with topics they didn’t recognize.

That leaves some learners with an awkward choice. They can carry on from where Duolingo says they are and hope the missing pieces eventually make sense, or they can reset the course and slog back through material they learned years ago. That second option is even less appealing now for free users affected by Duolingo’s Energy system, which limits how quickly they can work through lessons unless they spend gems or switch to the paid version. They have one other choice: to finally ditch the app, and there certainly seems to be some enthusiasm for that option.

There is also a separate but related frustration bubbling up around Unit Review. One Reddit user said they were considering canceling their subscription because their Unit Review had been replaced with flash cards that were too strict about acceptable answers. Personally, I couldn’t agree more with that gripe, as it’s one I share. Flashcards are a reasonable idea in theory, but when you pronounce a word and it gets marked as incorrect, you then hear the app provide the correct pronunciation. When that reveal sounds exactly like the noise you made, it’s hard not to simmer with frustration and shout “that’s what I said!” at your phone.

Duolingo announced in April that nine of its major courses had been expanded to reach a Duolingo Score of 129, which it says aligns with B2 on the CEFR scale. Those courses include Spanish, French, German, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Chinese, Portuguese, and English. That may at least explain why some courses look different or expanded, and a few learners in the Reddit threads liked that the course gave them more material to keep moving forward. However, it’s hardly a full justification for what many users see as an almost random reshuffling of progress.

# I Used to Love Duolingo, but It's Fallen So Far in These 5 Ways
...
I use Duolingo every day to learn French and have done so for over five years now. That’s why it pains me to see how far it’s fallen.

The service used to be the go-to app for learning a language, but too many issues have slowly taken away Duolingo’s edge over the competition.

Sorry, Duo, but you’re just not good enough anymore.

## 1. Duolingo Took Away Its Learning Tree

This was the big change that turned many users against Duolingo. People haven’t stopped complaining about this dumb decision, and neither should they; Duolingo made a huge mistake but has refused to acknowledge it as such.

Duolingo used to have a “learning tree” with a central trunk that branched off into many different lessons.

Couldn’t grasp a particular challenge? Just switch over to a different one and come back to it. Wanted some variety in your day so you’re not spending too long finding out about conjugations? No problem: you can learn more practical things like asking where the nearest restroom is.

This variety of choice meant Duolingo was fun and addictive. Then everything changed.

A major app update meant the learning tree was chopped down and replaced with a tedious, linear structure that you simply can’t escape from.

You don’t have options anymore: follow one set path… and that’s it. There’s nothing creative or educational about this method and it’s meant that Duolingo has become a chore.

## 2. Challenges Need More Gems

So what if you do want a bit of variety? You can check out other challenges, notably Match Madness and, at the weekends, the Ramp-Up Challenge.

The former lets you pair up words from your native language with ones you’ve learned in previous lessons. That runs across weekdays and each tier gets more difficult as the timer runs down. The XP rewards increase, however, and doubly so if you use an Early Bird or Night Owl Chest!

The Ramp-Up Challenge similarly increases XP while limiting timers.

These are great fun, but they’ll cost you. The cost used to be 30 gems each, so you had to save up a serious number of gems to access these games regularly. Then things got worse: the number of gems needed for each tier of these challenges went up.

They no longer cost 30 gems. They now cost 100 gems each.

That’s a massive increase—designed to push out underappreciated users who just want to learn a new language bit by bit. Of course, they don’t cost any gems if you’ve paid out for Super Duolingo or Duolingo Max, the premium versions of the service.

## 3. Duolingo Closed Its Forums

One of the great things about learning a language is becoming part of a new community. Duolingo used to revel in that, but not anymore.

If an answer doesn’t make sense, you could turn to the forums to clear up any confusion. It was really useful, especially if you didn’t know a native speaker of the language you’re trying to learn.

Those forums closed in 2022, and though sentence discussions—literally conversations about individual translations—were meant to stay archived and available for reference. Sadly, this archive was also shut down soon after. Some argue that it’s because the communities were pointing out mistakes in Duolingo’s lessons.

Some users have stepped up and created their own replacements. DuoMe has its own streak hall of fame and discussion boards, set up “to help […] rebuild what was lost with [the] old forum closing.” Still, Duolingo itself let us down.

## 4. Duolingo Is Now Just a Game

This is the biggest problem with the changes made to Duolingo. It feels less like a language-learning app and more like a game.

Can you beat today’s lesson? Can you climb the leaderboard? Can you do better than your friends?

One of the ways Duolingo became more like a game is through the leaderboards, weekly competitions with strangers to advance from Bronze to Sapphire, Amethyst to Diamond. There are 10 leagues in total and if you don’t get enough XP to stay in your current one or be promoted, you’ll drop back down.

Yes, that works for some people. I love gamification. But the focus here should really be on learning, not doing better than someone else halfway across the world.

Games are great, but Duolingo now relies too much on gaming techniques. It’s too tempting to do some quick, easy lessons to boost your XP instead of...

# Duolingo refond ses cours et se met une bonne partie de ses utilisateurs à dos

## Ce qu’il faut retenir Résumé généré par IA

- Duolingo a refondu neuf cours de langues (français, espagnol, allemand, italien, japonais et autres) en avril pour atteindre le niveau B2, mais la réorganisation a détraqué la progression des utilisateurs, renvoyant des apprenants avancés vers des leçons de débutant.
- Le nouveau système de révision par cartes applique des critères tellement stricts qu'il refuse des bonnes réponses, et la reconnaissance vocale recale des phrases correctes, rendant l'expérience frustrante.
- Duolingo a ajouté un système d'énergie limitant les exercices gratuits, ce qui agace les utilisateurs et pousse certains à envisager de résilier, comme cela s'était déjà produit l'an dernier avec sa stratégie IA.

Duolingo pensait sans doute faire plaisir à ses apprenants en musclant ses cours, et c'est plutôt l'inverse qui se produit. Depuis la refonte de neuf de ses cours de langues, une partie de la communauté râle très fort.

L'idée de départ n'était pourtant pas mauvaise. En avril, l'application a annoncé étoffer neuf grosses langues, dont le français, l'espagnol, l'allemand, l'italien et le japonais, pour permettre d'atteindre un niveau B2, soit un bon niveau intermédiaire avancé sur l'échelle européenne.

Sauf que ça ne s'est pas passé comme prévu, en réorganisant l'intégralité du parcours, Duolingo a aussi pas mal mélangé la progression des gens. Des utilisateurs très avancés, certains niveau 50 en italien, se sont retrouvés renvoyés vers des leçons de grand débutant incapable de commander une pizza au resto.

Le résultat est franchement incohérent par endroits. Des unités marquées comme terminées contiennent des notions jamais croisées, pendant que des leçons ajoutées après coup sont considérées comme déjà maîtrisées.

Le nouveau système de cartes de révision n'arrange d'ailleurs pas grand chose, avec des critères tellement stricts qu'une bonne réponse peut se voir refusée, et la reconnaissance vocale en rajoute une couche en recalant à l'oral des phrases pourtant correctes.

En plus de tout ce bordel, Duolingo a mis en place un système d'énergie, une sorte de jauge de vies limitées comme dans un jeu mobile, qui rationne le nombre d'exercices gratuits et agace encore plus ceux qui voulaient juste réviser tranquillement.

Beaucoup de membres parlent carrément de résilier leur abonnement.

Ce n'est pas la première fois que la marque se fâche avec son public, puisque l'an dernier déjà, sa stratégie tout IA, quitte à remplacer des humains par des machines, avait provoqué un tollé qui l'avait forcée à rétropédaler.

Vouloir pousser ses élèves plus loin, c'est une bonne idée, mais renvoyer un joueur niveau 50 réapprendre à dire bonjour, c'est le meilleur moyen de le faire filer chez la concurrence.

Source : Clubic

results.title: Duolingo has angered millions of users. A major update has ruined courses and years of study - Duolingo is one of the most popular language learning apps in the world, regularly adding new features and extensive course modi...
results.summary:
Duolingo is one of the most popular language learning apps in the world, regularly adding new features and extensive course modifications. But instead of positive reactions, its latest major update has sparked a wave of criticism. Many users complain that the app changed their study plan virtually overnight, moved them to different lessons, or started presenting them with material they never learned.

These are not isolated cases. Similar experiences are reported by students of Italian, German, Spanish, Japanese and other languages in the application. Duolingo And this raises the question of whether the update was sufficiently prepared from the perspective of the users themselves.

## Duolingo progress disappeared

The biggest problem is that Duolingo adjusted the course structure. The application has maintained the progress achieved, but the content of the individual lessons has changed. The result is a situation where some users they repeat the very basics, while others assume knowledge of vocabulary or grammar that they have never passed.

For studying a foreign language, it is continuity one of the most important factors. If individual lessons do not follow each other logically, learning can be significantly more challenging and at the same time demotivating. Many users describingthat she lost confidence in her knowledge because the application suddenly required working with new vocabulary without prior explanation.

## Expanding courses should have been a step forward

The changes were not made without reason. Duolingo has grown significantly in recent months. expanded several of the largest language coursesto offer more content up to a level corresponding to approximately B2 according to the European Framework of Reference. This is undoubtedly positive news for new users and those who want to continue using the application longer than before.

The problem arises when new content is inserted into already developed learning paths. Instead of a smooth continuation, some students have their lesson order completely changed, which can disrupt long-term habits.

## New cards also drew criticism

The dissatisfaction is not limited to the courses themselves. Another wave of criticism on Reddit and other forums is directed at revised review lessons using flashcards. According to users, they are much stricter in evaluating correct answers and often reject pronunciation or wording that is factually correct.

People expect a certain level of tolerance when it comes to language apps. Pronunciation can vary slightly depending on accent or phone microphone, and overly strict evaluation can be more of an obstacle than a motivation for further study.

## Duolingo seeks balance

Similar situations are not uncommon for large online services. Applications with millions of active users They regularly change algorithms, add new content, or modify the way they work with data. But each such change also affects people who have developed their own study routines over months or years.

Duolingo has long been betting on frequent updates and experimentation with new features. This helps the company develop the application, but at the same time increases the risk that some changes will be introduced too quickly or without sufficient communication to existing users.

It is not yet clear whether the company will respond to the criticism by further modifying the courses or offering the option of easier customization of the learning path. What is certain is that continuity of learning is one of the most important features of any language platform. If users lose it, they may start looking for alternatives, regardless of how much time they have already invested in their studies.

results.summary:
Duolingo patří mezi nejpopulárnější aplikace pro výuku jazyků na světě a pravidelně přidává nové funkce i rozsáhlé úpravy jednotlivých kurzů. Poslední velká aktualizace ale místo pozitivních reakcí vyvolala vlnu kritiky. Mnoho uživatelů si stěžuje, že jim aplikace prakticky přes noc změnila studijní plán, přesunula je do jiných lekcí nebo jim začala předkládat látku, kterou se nikdy neučili.

Nejde přitom o izolované případy. Podobné zkušenosti hlásí studenti italštiny, němčiny, španělštiny, japonštiny i dalších jazyků v aplikaci Duolingo. A právě to vyvolává otázku, zda byla aktualizace dostatečně připravena z pohledu samotných uživatelů.

## Pokrok v Duolingo zmizel

Největší problém spočívá v tom, že Duolingo upravilo strukturu kurzů. Aplikace sice zachovala dosažený postup, jenže obsah jednotlivých lekcí se změnil. Výsledkem je situace, kdy někteří uživatelé opakují úplné základy, zatímco jiným systém předpokládá znalosti slovíček nebo gramatiky, které nikdy neprošli.

Pro studium cizího jazyka je přitom návaznost jedním z nejdůležitějších faktorů. Pokud na sebe jednotlivé lekce logicky nenavazují, může být učení výrazně náročnější a zároveň demotivující. Řada uživatelů popisuje, že ztratila jistotu ve svých znalostech, protože aplikace náhle vyžaduje práci s novou slovní zásobou bez předchozího vysvětlení.

## Rozšíření kurzů mělo být krokem vpřed

Změny přitom nevznikly bez důvodu. Duolingo v posledních měsících výrazně rozšířilo několik největších jazykových kurzů, aby nabízely více obsahu až do úrovně odpovídající přibližně B2 podle evropského referenčního rámce. To je bezpochyby pozitivní zpráva pro nové uživatele i ty, kteří chtějí v aplikaci pokračovat déle než dříve.

Problém nastává ve chvíli, kdy se nový obsah vloží do již rozpracovaných studijních cest. Místo plynulého pokračování se některým studentům kompletně změnilo pořadí lekcí, což může narušit dlouhodobě budované návyky.

## Kritiku schytaly i nové kartičky

Nespokojenost se netýká pouze samotných kurzů. Další vlna kritiky na Redditu a jiných fórech směřuje na přepracované opakovací lekce využívající kartičky. Podle uživatelů jsou mnohem přísnější při hodnocení správných odpovědí a často odmítají výslovnost nebo formulace, které jsou fakticky správné.

Právě u jazykových aplikací přitom lidé očekávají určitou míru tolerance. Výslovnost se může mírně lišit podle přízvuku nebo mikrofonu telefonu a příliš striktní vyhodnocování může být spíše překážkou než motivací k dalšímu studiu.

## Duolingo hledá rovnováhu

Podobné situace nejsou u velkých online služeb ničím výjimečným. Aplikace s miliony aktivních uživatelů pravidelně mění algoritmy, přidávají nový obsah nebo upravují způsob práce s daty. Každá taková změna ale zároveň zasahuje lidi, kteří si během měsíců nebo let vytvořili vlastní studijní rutinu.

Duolingo dlouhodobě sází na časté aktualizace a experimentování s novými funkcemi. To firmě pomáhá aplikaci rozvíjet, zároveň však roste riziko, že některé změny budou zavedeny příliš rychle nebo bez dostatečné komunikace směrem ke stávajícím uživatelům.

Zatím není jasné, zda společnost na kritiku zareaguje další úpravou kurzů nebo nabídne možnost jednoduššího přizpůsobení studijní cesty. Jisté ale je, že právě kontinuita výuky patří mezi nejdůležitější vlastnosti každé jazykové platformy. Pokud ji uživatelé ztratí, mohou začít hledat alternativy bez ohledu na to, kolik času do svého studia už investovali.

results.title: The Duolingo French Course Changes: Everything You Must Know - The Duolingo French Course Changes: Everything You Must Know
results.summary:
Here’s a simple breakdown of the old system versus the new one:

- The Old “Tree”: A branching structure of skill “bubbles.” You could choose to level up different skills (e.g., “Food,” “Present Tense,” “Family”) independently. You could also easily go back to a specific, early skill to practice it without affecting your progress on others.
- The New “Path”: A single, linear track you follow from top to bottom. Skills, stories, and practice sessions are interspersed in a fixed order determined by Duolingo. You can’t skip ahead, and reviewing past topics requires you to scroll back down the path to find that specific lesson “circle.”

For me, I remember the freedom of the old tree. If I felt my knowledge of the passé composé was weak, I could spend a whole day just strengthening that one skill. The new path makes that kind of targeted practice more cumbersome.

### Why Did Duolingo Make This Change?

Duolingo’s official stance is that the new path is based on learning science. Their internal data suggested that a guided path would be more effective for keeping learners on track and ensuring they were practicing the right material at the right time. The key reasons cited were:

- Spaced Repetition: The path is designed to automatically re-introduce concepts at intervals that are supposed to be optimal for memory.
- Reduced “Choice Paralysis”: For new learners, the old tree could be intimidating. The new path offers a clear “what’s next,” removing the guesswork.
- Integrated Content: It allowed Duolingo to more seamlessly weave in its “Stories” and other features directly into the curriculum, rather than having them siloed in separate tabs.

### Is the New French Path Better or Worse? A Balanced Look

This is the million-dollar question, and the answer honestly depends on your learning style. There isn’t a universally “better” version; there are just different philosophies. Many veteran learners expressed frustration, while some newcomers find the structure helpful.

Aspect | The New Path: Pros | The New Path: Cons 
---|---|---
Structure | Clear, guided progression. No confusion about what to do next. | Rigid and linear. Restricts learner freedom and autonomy. 
Review | Spaced repetition is built-in, theoretically optimizing practice. | Difficult to target and practice specific weak skills on demand. 
Pacing | Consistent and methodical. Good for building a steady habit. | Can feel slow and repetitive if you already know a topic well. 
For Beginners | Less intimidating, very straightforward to start. | May not understand the “why” behind the lesson order. 
For Intermediate/Advanced | Ensures no gaps in knowledge are accidentally left behind. | Extremely frustrating. Inability to skip or focus on specific advanced topics. 

### Can I Go Back to the Old Duolingo French Tree?

Unfortunately, the answer is a simple and direct “no.” The rollout of the new learning path was a permanent, platform-wide update that was completed for all users by late 2022. There is no setting or workaround to revert your account to the old tree interface. The path is now the standard Duolingo experience.

## Content & Quality Shifts: Grammar, Voices, and More

Beyond the structural changes, the content of the French course itself has evolved. This includes how grammar is taught, the voices you hear, and the overall effectiveness of the curriculum.

### Did They Remove Grammar Notes from the French Course?

This is one of the most common and panicked questions from users of the new path. No, the grammar notes were not removed, but they were moved and renamed, making them harder to find. What used to be “Tips” are now called “Guidebooks.”

Here’s how to find them:

- On the learning path, tap on a unit’s title header (e.g., “Unit 5: Order food and drinks”).
- A pop-up will appear, and you’ll see a “Guidebook” icon or button.
- Tap the Guidebook. It contains the key vocabulary and grammar explanations for that entire unit.

While the content is still there, many feel it’s less convenient than the old system, where tips were attached to each individual lesson bubble. Now, you get a larger info dump for the whole unit at once.

### Why Do the French Voices Sound So Different?

If you’ve noticed the characters’ voices have changed over the years, you’re not imagining it. Duolingo has been transitioning from using human voice actors for its core sentences to more advanced, proprietary Text-to-Speech (TTS) technology.

results.summary:
Duolingo är en av de mest populära språkinlärningsapparna i världen och lägger regelbundet till nya funktioner och omfattande kursändringar. Men istället för positiva reaktioner har den senaste stora uppdateringen utlöst en våg av kritik. Många användare klagar på att appen ändrade deras studieplan praktiskt taget över en natt, flyttade dem till andra lektioner eller började presentera material de aldrig lärde sig.

Detta är inte isolerade fall. Liknande erfarenheter rapporteras av studenter i italienska, tyska, spanska, japanska och andra språk på Duolingo . Och detta väcker frågan om uppdateringen var tillräckligt förberedd ur användarnas egna perspektiv.

## Duolingos framsteg försvann

Det största problemet är att Duolingo har ändrat strukturen på sina kurser . Medan appen har bibehållit de framsteg som gjorts, har innehållet i varje lektion ändrats. Resultatet är att vissa användare upprepar de allra grundläggande sakerna , medan systemet för andra förutsätter kunskaper i ordförråd eller grammatik som de aldrig har behärskat.

När man lär sig ett främmande språk är konsekvens en av de viktigaste faktorerna. Om de enskilda lektionerna inte följer logiskt på varandra kan inlärningen bli betydligt mer utmanande och demotiverande. Många användare beskriver att de tappar förtroendet för sina kunskaper eftersom applikationen plötsligt kräver att man arbetar med nya ord utan föregående förklaring.
...
## Att utöka kurserna var tänkt att vara ett steg framåt

Förändringarna är inte utan anledning. Under de senaste månaderna har Duolingo avsevärt utökat flera av sina största språkkurser för att erbjuda mer innehåll upp till ungefär B2- nivå enligt den gemensamma europeiska referensramen för språk. Detta är utan tvekan positiva nyheter för nya användare och de som vill fortsätta använda appen längre än tidigare.

Problemet uppstår när nytt innehåll infogas i redan utvecklade lärvägar. Istället för en smidig fortsättning får vissa elever sin lektionsordning helt ändrad, vilket kan störa långsiktiga vanor.

## Nya kort fick också kritik

Missnöjet är inte begränsat till själva kurserna. En annan våg av kritik på Reddit och andra forum riktas mot de omdesignade flashcard-recensionslektionerna . Enligt användare är de mycket strängare i att utvärdera korrekta svar och avvisar ofta uttal eller formuleringar som är sakligt korrekta.

Folk förväntar sig en viss nivå av tolerans när det gäller språkappar. Uttalet kan variera något beroende på accent eller telefonmikrofon, och alltför strikt betygsättning kan vara mer ett hinder än en motivation för vidare studier.

## Duolingo söker balans

Sådana situationer är inte ovanliga för stora onlinetjänster. Appar med miljontals aktiva användare ändrar regelbundet algoritmer, lägger till nytt innehåll eller modifierar hur de arbetar med data. Men varje sådan förändring påverkar också personer som har utvecklat sina egna studierutiner under månader eller år.

Duolingo har länge förlitat sig på frekventa uppdateringar och experiment med nya funktioner. Detta hjälper företaget att utveckla appen, men samtidigt finns det en växande risk att vissa ändringar introduceras för snabbt eller utan tillräcklig kommunikation till befintliga användare.

Det är ännu inte klart om företaget kommer att svara på kritiken genom att ytterligare modifiera kurserna eller erbjuda möjligheten att enklare anpassa inlärningsvägen. Det som är säkert är att kontinuitet i lärandet är en av de viktigaste funktionerna hos alla språkplattformar. Om användarna förlorar den kan de börja leta efter alternativ, oavsett hur mycket tid de redan har investerat i sina studier.

results.title: Adiós, Duolingo Spanish!
results.summary:
# Adiós, Duolingo Spanish!
...
I woke up to a huge surprise on Saturday morning, September 26, 2026. Duolingo ran an update when I turned my android phone on. After opening the Duolingo app I noticed I was positioned somewhere on the path I was not at night before. I should have been in Section 2, Unit 16 “Describe your routine”. I have transcribed sentences and grammatical explanations from 75% of that unit. I scrolled around and realized this was a different version of the learning path for Latin American Spanish.

I went all the way back to Section 1, Unit 1. The vocabulary had changed. Now in addition to words for tea (té), coffee (café), and milk (leche) in Spanish, we also had words for dog (perro) and cat (gato). Other lessons had vocabulary I had never seen before. I noticed there were more colorful elements like verdad added early on. This made the sentences with it sound more conversational and less automated. I skipped ahead and found some lessons were outside what I had previously learned. To accurately answer questions, understand things in a logical progression and qualify for XP I would have to start at the beginning. It made no sense to me to guess or skip ahead.

The grammar notes in Duolingo’s latest Spanish update contain run-on words.

The fun started when I checked the grammar notes you can access by clicking on the notepad icon in the header with the unit name. Many words were run together as if one word. “Mi maleta” (my suitcase) is shown as “mimaleta” and “mi abuelo” (my grandfather) shows as “miabuelo”. The students just starting out with the new Latin American Spanish course are not gaining quality content. What they are getting is the product of a deeply flawed company that can no longer gloss over the screw-ups it puts out as releases. All the engagement farming which grants higher XP for longer periods of time on the app is no compensation at all. It is a cynical trick to breed an addiction-like craving to exceed the previous amount of XP gained. This is when learning is degraded and the value of one’s time and effort is trashed.

My complaint to Duolingo was written in English. The reply I received was in Turkish.

I also study Turkish and Dutch. The Turkish course might explain why my complaint to Duolingo was answered in Turkish, even though I wrote my complaint in English. There was no announcement about this change, so I went to Gemini for information. What I learned is that Duolingo releases updates that conform to the CEFR. I agree that standardizing the course is a good thing. I question, though how long Duolingo can stretch its educational side. Is this a game or is it a serious language course? For casual students who want to learn both a language and engage in the game, less changes and less standardization is necessary. However, for serious students the entire approach should be different. I am thinking of the excellent A1 and A2 Dutch material published by Kleurrijker for the TaalCompleet series. Or BOOM Uitgever’s In Zicht series. Duolingo puts one foot in each world, and it is increasignly failing to live up to either.

This is to be expected from a company that has let go of the humans who guide AI in all operations. AI is not intelligent or sentient. It is a mirror of the person using and directing it. Given what I experienced, and the customer service reply I received, I’d say nobody at Duolingo is minding AI and everyone, including Luis van Ahn, is asleep at the wheel.

I’ve moved to Babbel for Latin American Spanish courses and am using Gemini to filter through the sometimes dense layering in those lessons. Babbel has a way of introducing advanced concepts early on. Verb tenses and pronouns more suitable to A2 pop up in A1 level lessons. I prompt Gemini to review documents containing screen shots or sentence transcriptions from the Babbel lessons. Among my criteria are to extract the core grammar and principles that are most important for me at the current A1 level I am at. Then Gemini creates bulleted lists and summaries about what is pertienent. From there I ask Gemini to test my learning with online quizzes and exercises I do off-line.

Duolingo is pushing the structure of its most popular courses like Spanish to more advanced levels like B1 and B2. As tempting as that is for me, I will not go back. I will use Babbel to go as far as I can to complete A2 level. Then I’ll decide on the next steps.

results.title: Giving up on Duolingo
results.summary:
## Giving up on Duolingo
...
I had been using Duolingo for years, as I created my account 11 years ago. I casually started using it hoping to pick up some Spanish. I fell off it for a while after having a streak of 500+ days, then came back to it more seriously and kept things going for much longer.
...
This ended last month, as I willingly gave up on my streak of nearly 2100 days and stopping doing practice runs. I uninstalled the app the same day from everywhere to make sure I'd be free of the Owl's notifications.
...
There's a multitude of things that led me to this point, really. The first truth, and one that it took me a long time to acknowledge, is that what the app is in 2025 isn't what I liked in 2015 or even 2020. One of the most useful feature was the user forums, where you could read discussions on each lesson and sometimes better understand why you made an error... or why a specific answer could've been acceptable to a human speaker. These were removed a few years ago. Likewise, some lessons included optional grammar tips, helping you put into context the vocabulary you were about to learn. The learning system was also changed from a tree of sorts, with multiple options, to a purely linear one. The old system allowed you to choose between a few lessons, even if you needed to complete them all to pass some gate. This choice was removed, so I couldn't make a decision based on what I was feeling like doing at the moment. The linear path also felt endless, even if it was the same length in practice.

Beyond that was a general frustration after reading several articles on how the Duolingo founder and CEO wanted to go all-in on AI, replacing the company's volunteers and contractors with automated systems. Language is a highly human subject and AI can't get this right at the moment, especially when it comes to regional nuances or things that could be properly understood by a subset of speakers.

The kicker? For the past 2-3 years, I've been a paying user of the app. I wanted to remove the obnoxious ads, sure, but I also wanted to support a model that I rather liked. That model was changed bit-by-bit, until it was no longer something I agreed with. Even worse, the company introduced a new, higher tier of subscription and they were trying to sell to me pretty much every day. If I'm paying to remove the ads, I don't want different ads to take their place, no matter how relevant they can be. I think my breaking point happened when one of the ads for the higher tier simulated a phone call, including making my phone ring and vibrate. That's a very big no-no to me, and the second time it happened, I pretty much checked out of the thing.

The final confirmation? One day, I learned that I had access to a different language learning tool thanks to my library card. I logged in and used their classification test, curious to see how well I'd do after spending several years on Duolingo. That test ranked me as beginner and sent me to lesson 1A – Greetings. That's when I knew I was done and uninstalled everything, even if I was only midway through my paid year.

Was this all a big waste? I want to say no. I've learned a lot of vocabulary and I can now understand some sentences when people are speaking. I've clearly picked up some of the language, even if my phrasing is probably terrible. I didn't hate it either. The simple truth is that the Duolingo of 2025 is not the 2015 tool I liked, and it took me quite a while to realize it and move on. Adios!

– Doctacosa
